title: Compactified direct-image towers, reduction and composition
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ and choose compactifications $c=(j,\bar f)$, where $j$ is quasi-compact open, $\bar f$ proper and $f=\bar f j$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $F_f^c=R\bar f_*j_!$, with integral and field realizations exactly as in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. On the finite bounded-below etale-origin domain (a chosen pullback from the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]), the canonical refinement maps between the $F_f^c$ are isomorphisms, independent of a common refinement, with identity and transitivity cocycles. Bounded constructible finite inputs admit these witnesses. These same normalized comparisons hold on integral constructible inputs with compatible finite-reduction witnesses and on their specified lattice and common-stage field presentations; they respect reduction and coefficient passage.
For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ put $K_n=K\otimes_R^L A_n$. The canonical reduction maps are isomorphisms
$$(Rf_*K)\otimes_R^L A_n\simeq Rf_{*,n}K_n,\qquad (Rf_!K)\otimes_R^L A_n\simeq Rf_{!,n}K_n.$$
For $A_n\to A_m$ both direct-image comparisons are isomorphisms on $\mathcal C_{X,A_n}$. For a coherent normalized DVR tower $(M_n)$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], the actual counit gives $(R\varprojlim\operatorname{Res}_nM_n)\otimes_R^L A_m\simeq M_m$; if its terms are constructible in one common finite cohomological interval, its limit is in $D^b_c(Y,R)$.
The canonical composition maps give $R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$, satisfy identity and associativity, and agree with the specified completed and field composition maps. For proper $f$, the compactification with identity open factor gives the canonical identification $Rf_!\simeq Rf_*$, and under it the compact-support exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of [def-exchange-projection] is the proper base-change exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_*$. At the integral stage it identifies the strict quotient-transition tower defining compact support with the strict tower defining ordinary direct image, including transitions, and hence identifies their derived limits. Rational and common-stage passage carry that identification to the field stages.

proof.text: At a finite stage every bounded intrinsically constructible pro-etale complex has a bounded constructible etale origin by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Choose such a witness when one is not already part of the input. If the input has finite Tor amplitude, [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) gives the same amplitude for its etale origin. Thus the witnessed domain used below includes the bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs, and the etale and pro-etale finite-Tor conventions agree on them.

source.place: For (2): finite witnessed domain; Stacks proetale comparison, as exposed by the cited origin and Tor-amplitude statements.

proof.text: For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, apply [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] on the stated bounded-below etale-origin domain. It identifies its comparison with proper composition followed by $R\bar f_{2*}(Ru_*j_{1!}\simeq j_{2!})$, asserts invertibility, and gives identity and transitivity. Its common-refinement assertion gives independence and the triple cocycle. In particular if $t_i:F_f^d\simeq F_f^{c_i}$ come from one common refinement, the comparison is $t_2t_1^{-1}$ and $(t_3t_2^{-1})(t_2t_1^{-1})=t_3t_1^{-1}$. All functors here are restricted to the witnessed domain.

source.place: For (2): compactification comparisons; current prop-compactification-coherence proof, all three comparison paragraphs.

proof.text: For the canonical quotient $A_n\to A_m$, $1\leq m\leq n$, the ring $A_m$ is finite as an $A_n$-module, being generated by $1$. Apply [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] with $A=A_n$, $B=A_m$ to the finite-Tor origin of Step 1; its pro-etale conclusion identifies the actual counit-defined ordinary coefficient map as an isomorphism. Apply [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] to the same input for compact support. The former statement includes the successive-coefficient and direct-image-composition equations; the latter includes successive reductions and the counit compatibility. These are the stipulated finite coefficient maps, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their endpoints.

source.place: The ordinary finite quotient comparison is lem-coef-finite-direct-image; For (2), finite quotient compact-support coefficient change.

proof.text: For integral $K$, [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] gives $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ and precisely the canonical isomorphism $(Rf_*K)\otimes_R^LA_n\simeq Rf_{*,n}K_n$. For compact support use [lem-fix-operation-reduction] on its integral constructible domain. The identification with the specified tower definition is [lem-fix-compactification-completed-realization]: its $d_c$ identifies $R\bar f_{*,R}j_!K$ with $Rf_!^cK$ including quotient transitions, and its reduction is the ordered proper projection/open-tensor comparison. Hence the compact-support map is the canonical reduction isomorphism $(Rf_!K)\otimes_R^LA_n\simeq Rf_{!,n}K_n$. The integral constructibility of this output is [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible]. No finite-Tor hypothesis on the integral input is inserted.

source.place: For (2): integral reduction, using the completed compactification realization; Bhatt-Scholze 6.7.2 and 6.7.6-6.7.7 are the background for the cited constructibility nodes.

proof.text: For the coherent normalized system $(M_n)$ in the statement apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] directly. Its hypotheses are exactly the coherent transitions and invertible transition-adjoint comparisons in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. It gives the actual counit $M\otimes_R^LA_m\to M_m$, where $M=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$, as a coherent isomorphism, and makes $M$ derived complete. This use does not assume constructibility or boundedness.

source.place: Normalized tower reconstruction is lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity, with its actual counit normalization.

proof.text: If all $M_n$ are constructible with cohomology in $[a,b]$, the counit isomorphisms of Step 5 make every finite reduction of $M$ constructible with cohomology in that same interval. Together with the completeness already proved, these are exactly the membership conditions in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Thus $M\in D^b_c(Y,R)$. The bound concerns all reductions, and does not assert a new finiteness theorem from an unnormalized tower.

source.place: Normalized tower reconstruction: uniform finite-level bounds supply the integral constructible output.

proof.text: At a finite stage [thm-sf-comp-composition] gives the specified isomorphism $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\to R(gf)_!$, preservation of the bounded-below etale-origin class, independence of compactifications, its identity normalization and its associativity equation. Use $\alpha_{g,f}^{-1}$ if the comparison is written in the opposite direction as in this item. Inverting a commuting diagram of isomorphisms preserves its equality, so this direction change retains both the unit and associativity equations.

source.place: Clause (3) follows from thm-sf-comp-composition: finite composition and its coherence.

proof.text: For the strict-tower arguments put $I=(\varpi)\subset R$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R$ is a DVR, hence Noetherian; $I$ is generated by one element. [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] gives finite perfect $A_n$, with resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R]$. The residue field has characteristic $\ell$: $\ell$ has absolute value less than $1$, and integers prime to $\ell$ are units. Thus $R/I$ is additive torsion. These check the coefficient hypotheses of the completion and word-realization lemmas. Each scheme in a compactification or compatible tower is finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since the field $k$ is Noetherian. In particular its open immersions are quasi-compact, as required by the proper/open calculus.

source.place: For (2) and Clause (3): coefficient and geometric hypotheses for the strict-tower realization argument.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to work in complete constant-$R$ coordinates; it preserves finite reductions, quotient transitions, total limits and completion units. In those coordinates [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit] supplies $a_W:W_cK\simeq R\lim(\widetilde W\mathcal RK)$ for every finite word in completed opens and direct images, with $q_{VW}=(\widetilde Vq_W)q_V$. Its hypotheses were checked in Step 8 and it requires no uniform Tor interval. [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identifies its direct-image generator and strict coefficient transitions with the completed-sheaf direct image. [lem-fix-compactification-completed-realization] identifies the two-letter word with exactly $F_f^c$ of the statement. Consequently nested compact-support operations have specified comparisons with their whole strict words, with the same vertex map at each occurrence of an intermediate object.

source.place: For (2) and composition in Clause (3): completed word realization; strict-diagram argument of fix-lem-exchanges, integral refinement/composition paragraphs.

proof.text: Write $P_p$ for strict-tower derived direct image, $J_j$ for termwise open extension and $N=\mathcal RK$. For $u:c_1\to c_2$, use the square $Q_u=(r=1_X,p=u,k=j_1,i=j_2)$. [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] gives an invertible normalized map $\gamma_{Q_u}:J_{j_2}\to P_uJ_{j_1}$ on $N$, with exactly the finite refinement normalization. Define $\rho_u:P_{p_1}J_{j_1}N\simeq P_{p_2}P_uJ_{j_1}N\xrightarrow{P_{p_2}\gamma_{Q_u}^{-1}}P_{p_2}J_{j_2}N$. The identity and vertical-pasting equations of that calculus give $\rho_1=1$ and $\rho_{vu}=\rho_v\rho_u$ before evaluation. [prop-compactification-refinement] supplies common refinements and equalization of parallel refinements. Applying these to two common refinements makes their maps to both $c_i$ equal. Transitivity then identifies the expressions $\rho_2\rho_1^{-1}$; the same cancellation with three targets proves their cocycle in the strict derived category.

source.place: For (2): integral refinement independence, using strict proper/open pasting (Stacks Tags 0F7B and 0F7C, more-etale.tex).

proof.text: Apply the exact total-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to Step 10 and conjugate by the vertex maps $a_W$ of Step 9. For composable tower maps $U,V$, the two transported arrows multiply as $a_2^{-1}R\lim(V)a_1\,a_1^{-1}R\lim(U)a_0=a_2^{-1}R\lim(VU)a_0$. Thus invertibility, identity, transitivity, common-refinement independence and the cocycle hold integrally. The finite evaluations of the strict maps were fixed by Step 10; Step 9 fixes their reduction units and strict transitions, so their reductions are the finite comparisons of Step 2. The coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] preserve the units, counits and tensor comparisons defining these proper/open maps; substituting these comparisons in the formula for $\rho_u$ proves coefficient compatibility on the stated domains.

source.place: For (2): apply total derived limit to actual strict maps; retain normalized reductions and coefficient passage.

proof.text: Choose a compatible compactification tower for $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], using the compactifications and cofilteredness of [prop-compactification-refinement]. Write $Y\xrightarrow v\bar Y\xrightarrow bZ$, $X\xrightarrow a\bar X\xrightarrow p\bar Y$, $V=\bar X\times_{\bar Y}Y$, $t:V\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $r:V\to Y$ and $c:X\hookrightarrow V$, so $a=tc$. The square $Q=(r,p,t,v)$ is Cartesian. On strict towers the comparison is the explicit composite $P_bJ_vP_rJ_c\xrightarrow{P_b\gamma_QJ_c}P_bP_pJ_tJ_c\simeq P_{bp}J_{tc}$. [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] gives its invertibility: $J_cN$ has bounded-below etale-origin evaluations because [thm-sf-comp-composition] preserves that class, applied to the open map $c$. Its finite evaluations are the same proper/open composite constructing $\alpha_{g,f}$ of Step 7.

source.place: Clause (3): compact-support composition, Stacks Tag 0F7J, more-etale.tex, lemma-shriek-composition; compatible compactification diagram and proper/open composite.

proof.text: Refine two choices of the compatible tower to a common one as in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. Expanding the composite of Step 12, its comparison square is a pasting of the horizontal and vertical proper/open equations of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]; the open and proper compositors are the canonical ones in those equations. Thus it commutes with the $\rho$ of Step 10, giving independence of the tower. For three maps choose a nested compactification tower by successive applications of [prop-compactification-refinement]. Both parenthesizations start at the same six-letter strict word. Expand each by Step 12: the equations for adjacent rectangles are exactly horizontal/vertical pasting of $\gamma$ in the cited calculus, while transformations on disjoint letters commute by naturality. They therefore give the same arrow to the flattened two-letter word. The identity-square clauses give the identity when either map is an identity. This proves associativity and the unit equations as strict-derived equalities.

source.place: Clause (3): independence and associativity, Stacks more-etale.tex lemma-pseudo-functor and proper/open pasting laws, Tags 0F7C and 0F7D; strict-tower version is the cited calculus.

proof.text: Apply total derived limit to the strict composition map and the equations of Steps 12-13, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the word comparisons of Step 9 at its source and target, so the middle vertex cancels exactly as in Step 11. This gives $Rg_!Rf_!\simeq R(gf)_!$ with its identity and associativity equations on the integral category. The normalized concatenation formula of [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit] identifies its source with the nested completed functors, so it is their specified completed composition map. All intermediate compact-support objects belong to $D^b_c$ by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible]; no additional Tor bound is needed. The reduction of this composite is the finite composition map of Step 7, because all its strict proper/open factors have those specified evaluations.

source.place: Clause (3): completed composition from the strict map, including its normalization and constructible domain.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is proper and take $c_0=(1_X,f)$. By [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence], the finite canonical identification is $\alpha_{f,n}=Rf_{*,n}(a_X)$, where $a_X:(1_X)_!\simeq1$ is the identity-open identification. Thus $Rf_{!,n}^{c_0}\simeq Rf_{*,n}$. For any other compactification use the canonical comparison of Step 2 (or Step 11 integrally) with $c_0$; independence and its cocycle remove the auxiliary choice.

source.place: Clause (3): proper coincidence at the identity compactification, cor-cbc-proper-coincidence proof.

proof.text: The integral compact-support tower in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] has transition obtained by applying the finite functor to the quotient map, then coefficient restriction. For $c_0$, the identity-open identification $a_X$ is applied degreewise and commutes with every module map, including coefficient quotients. Replacing $(1_X)_!$ by $1$ in this strict construction therefore gives exactly the ordinary direct-image tower: its transition is $Rf_{*,n+1}$ of $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}K_n$, followed by the direct-image coefficient-restriction comparison. [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identifies this strict tower, including transitions and projections, with the one reconstructing $Rf_*K$. Taking total limit identifies $Rf_!K$ with $Rf_*K$. This is an identification of the actual specified strict towers, not an inference of equality from reductions of derived arrows.

source.place: Clause (3): proper coincidence at the integral stage, comparing the strict quotient-transition constructions.

proof.text: For finite etale coefficients the proper exchange equation under $\alpha_f,\alpha_{f'}$ is explicitly [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]. For witnessed finite pro-etale coefficients use the actual formula of [def-exchange-projection]: at $j=1_X$, its proper factor is $f$ and its open factor $\beta$ is the identity under $a_X,a_{X'}$. The displayed composite for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is consequently exactly $\operatorname{Ex}_*$, conjugated by these $\alpha$'s. Integrally [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] is likewise the proper completed mate followed by the completed open comparison. At the identity open the latter is the identity and $j_!K=K$, so the proper factor is the same specified completed exchange. The strict identification in Step 16 identifies its source and target towers and their transitions. Hence proper coincidence identifies the stipulated exchanges at the integral stage as well.

source.place: Clause (3): proper coincidence and exchange normalization at identity open factors, finite and completed formulas.

proof.text: Finally pass all integral functors and comparisons to the chosen lattice presentations over $E$ by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]: each transformation component is its integral component tensored with $1$, so the image of an inverse remains an inverse and every identity between composites remains an identity. Their compatibility with finite coefficient-field extension is supplied by [lem-fix-operation-reduction], including its preservation of the units, counits and coefficient comparisons constructing the maps above. [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] then descends these transformations and their equations to the common-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category. A finite diagram representing any refinement, composition or proper-exchange equation is taken at one common finite stage; enlargement preserves that equation. These are precisely the rational and common-stage functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], so they carry also the strict-tower proper identification of Step 16. Reduction compatibility always refers to the integral presentations and finite quotient domains; there is no reduction functor from $E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ to $A_n$.

lean.statement: theorem sfPackageCompactifiedTowerComparisons (X Y : SixFunctorSpace D) [IsSeparated X.obj.hom] [IsSeparated Y.obj.hom] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f.hom.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.hom.left] [QuasiCompact f.hom.left] : (∀ K : sixFunctorFiniteCategory D C E n hn X, ∃ O : RefinementFiniteLevelOrigin C.l E n hn X.obj.left, Nonempty ((sixFunctorFiniteRealization D C E n hn X).functor.obj (refinementFiniteLevelFixedObject C.l E n hn X.obj.left O) ≅ K.obj)) ∧ ∃ theta : ∀ (c d : Compactification f.hom.left) (_r : c ⟶ d), compactificationOriginCandidate C.l E n hn c ≅ compactificationOriginCandidate C.l E n hn d, (∀ (c d : Compactification f.hom.left) (r : c ⟶ d) (O : RefinementFiniteLevelOrigin C.l E n hn X.obj.left), (theta c d r).app O = refinementComparisonIsomorphism D.k C.l (sfPackageCoefficientIsUnit D C) E n hn f.hom.left r O) ∧ (∀ c : Compactification f.hom.left, theta c c (𝟙 c) = Iso.refl _) ∧ (∀ (c d e : Compactification f.hom.left) (r : c ⟶ d) (s : d ⟶ e), theta c e (r ≫ s) = theta c d r ≪≫ theta d e s) ∧ ∃ comparison : ∀ c d : Compactification f.hom.left, compactificationOriginCandidate C.l E n hn c ≅ compactificationOriginCandidate C.l E n hn d, (∀ (c d e : Compactification f.hom.left) (r : e ⟶ c) (s : e ⟶ d), comparison c d = (theta e c r).symm ≪≫ theta e d s) ∧ (∀ c d e : Compactification f.hom.left, comparison c d ≪≫ comparison d e = comparison c e)
